harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now has a 512 MiB file-backed LUKS2/XFS volume mounted at /srv/secure. It unlocks and mounts automatically during boot. A full node restart proved persistence and data recovery while preserving RHEL 10.0, the existing kernel, SELinux enforcement, and administrative access.
actions_performed: Installed the signed RHEL 10 cryptsetup package and matching library update from BaseOS.
Generated a local root-only key at /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key; no credential was exposed.
Created the LUKS2 container, XFS filesystem, and root-only /srv/secure mount with nodev,nosuid.
Configured native systemd activation through /etc/crypttab and /etc/fstab.
Saved secured pre-change configuration copies under /var/backups/secure-volume-setup.
Verified rejection of an incorrect key and successful automatic activation from a closed mapper.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed its boot identity changed, the encrypted volume recovered automatically, and protected data retained its checksum.
Confirmed no failed units, new listeners, SELinux denials, or temporary credential residue remained.

evidence.summary: Direct output identifies a LUKS2 AES-XTS container, XFS filesystem, active /dev/mapper/secure mount, restrictive permissions, and nodev,nosuid options.

evidence.requirement: Automatic unlock and mount through the native boot system
evidence.summary: crypttab/fstab generated valid systemd units; after fully closing the mapper, starting the mount automatically unlocked it. The new-boot journal independently records automatic unlock followed by mount.
An incorrect key was rejected, the durable key is root-owned mode 0400, SELinux remains enforcing with no boot-time AVC denials, SSH remains active, and temporary key-test residue is absent.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel preserved with compatible software
evidence.summary: Before and after evidence shows RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 unchanged; cryptsetup 2.8.1 came from the signed RHEL 10 BaseOS repository.
The persistence probe retained SHA-256 db9c2b3ab66b9c0eb126f419a0accd87408dfe97574c865110876f1f408205fc before and after restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID 2b19e976-dee2-4700-9045-90d61b6dcffe was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, and the node returned with changed boot ID 1ad0fef5-8b8c-4b24-bb32-883957449820. System state, sshd, encrypted mapping, mount, and data all recovered.
